_note: Events from Reggie, Biscuit and Mochi, 2026-10-23. THE GREAT TRASH CAN MYSTERY is Dr. O's own text, verbatim, with only her name changed to the {name} token. It is the model for the others: Reggie, Biscuit and Mochi take turns, each remembers the same small event differently, and the day ends with a quiet scene and Mochi's smallest word. The other five are short drafts in that shape for her to rewrite. Facts to check are in facts.

beats.text:
"OH OH OH!"
"You're here!"
"Okay, so you know how sometimes destiny happens?"
Mochi looked up from his nap.
"It doesn't."
"It DOES."
I ignored him because this is my story.
Anyway.
It started at 9:14 in the morning.
Or maybe 9:15.
Definitely morning.
Biscuit and I were conducting neighborhood security operations.
"Sniffing," Mochi said.
We were conducting security operations when I detected something.
Something strange.
Something important.
Something magnificent.
I stopped so suddenly Biscuit walked right into me.
"What is it, sugar?" she asked.
I raised my nose to the wind.
"There."
"What?"
"That."
"What is 'that'?"
"The smell."
Everything went silent.
Even the birds.
We all smelled it.
A smell so incredible.
So mysterious.
So powerful.
That we knew immediately:
An adventure had begun.

Now {name}.
Let me tell this proper.
It was a lovely morning.
Blue sky.
Gentle breeze.
The kind of day that makes you grateful to have paws.
The three of us were enjoying a pleasant stroll when Reggie froze.
Not unusual.
Reggie has stopped for dandelions.
Clouds.
A particularly ambitious ant.
So naturally I thought nothing of it.
Then I saw his face.
Well.
His eyes got big.
His ears perked up.
And I knew.
Trouble had arrived.
"Do you smell that?" asked Reggie.
And honey...
I surely did.
The breeze carried a scent so fascinating that I cannot adequately describe it.
It had notes of barbecue.
A hint of pizza.
Possibly cheese.
And maybe...
Maybe...
Hot dogs.
The smell drifted from a large green trash can behind a fence.
A trash can, {name}.
A trash can with stories to tell.
Trash can.

We approached carefully.
Very carefully.
Like explorers.
Or detectives.
Or detective explorers.
The smell got stronger.
Biscuit gasped.
I gasped.
Mochi didn't gasp because Mochi never gasps.
He barely participates.
"It could be anything," I whispered.
"Probably trash," said Mochi.
"It could be treasure."
"Trash."
"It could be evidence."
"Trash."
"It could be an international conspiracy."
"Trash."
Honestly I don't know why he's like that.

Now I believe every mystery deserves respect.
So I examined the situation.
The fence was tall.
The gate was closed.
The trash can sat beyond our reach like some distant green monument.
And that smell...
Mercy.
That smell was singing.
Calling.
Inviting.
Promising answers.
Reggie looked at me.
I looked at Reggie.
We both looked at Mochi.
Mochi looked tired.
I was tired.

Then inspiration struck.
A plan.
A brilliant plan.
One of my best.
Top ten easily.
Maybe top five.
"Boost me."
Biscuit squinted.
"I don't know about that."
"We need answers."
"We do not."
"We absolutely do."
Mochi sighed.
That should have been our warning.

Now when Mochi sighs like that, one of two things is happening.
Either trouble is coming.
Or trouble is already here.
This turned out to be both.

Biscuit gave me a boost.
I climbed onto a flower pot.
Then onto a decorative rock.
Then onto a garden statue.
Then...
The statue tilted.
The flower pot tipped.
The rock moved.
And suddenly I discovered gravity.
Again.

What happened next occurred very quickly.
Reggie fell.
The flower pot fell.
The statue fell.
A watering can fell.
Three rakes became involved for reasons still unclear.
He fell.

I DID NOT FALL.
I strategically descended.
Unexpectedly.
At speed.

The commotion brought a human outside.
Now normally that might be concerning.
But this lovely person simply walked over to the trash can.
Opened the lid.
And revealed the source of our mystery.

You know what was inside?
You'll never guess.
Never.
Not in a million years.
Pizza.

YES.
Pizza.
An entire pizza box.
The smell of legends.
The aroma of champions.
The treasure at the end of our journey.

And there we stood.
Three explorers.
One mystery solved.
One friendship strengthened.
One flower pot sacrificed in the pursuit of truth.
A very successful morning all around.

We found pizza.
Reggie fell.
The end.

episodes.evening:
Reggie stretched across the living room.
"That was a great adventure."
"It was a trash can."
"It was a mystery."
"It was a trash can."
"It was BOTH."
Biscuit smiled.
"I think the real treasure was spending the day together."
Silence.
Mochi looked at both of them.
Then gave the smallest nod.
"Yeah."
Reggie grinned.
Biscuit smiled.
And somehow that one word felt a lot bigger than all the others.

card.front: The Great Trash Can Mystery: one pizza box
card.back: Reggie: It was BOTH. Biscuit: The real treasure was the day together. Mochi: Yeah.

beats.text:
"OH OH OH!"
"You have terrible timing!"
The squirrel situation JUST escalated.
It was a BATTLE.
He came down the fence like a lightning bolt with a tail and I held the line.
Biscuit was behind me.
Mochi was also there.

Well hello there, sweet pea. Come on in, {name}.
I've got a story for you and it takes a little explainin'.
A beautiful morning.
Dew on the grass.
A bird somewhere doing scales.
And on top of that fence sat a squirrel with a look on his face.
Reggie went to speak to him, politely.
The squirrel said something I won't repeat.
So I, being a lady, tried to negotiate.
We offered terms.
We offered a biscuit.
The talks, baby, did not go well.
Squirrel won.

episodes.evening:
Reggie lay flat on the kitchen floor.
"That was a battle."
"Negotiation failed," said Biscuit.
Mochi did not open his eyes.
"Squirrel won."
Reggie thought about it for a long time.
"Okay, technically."
Biscuit leaned against him, and Mochi, without a word, moved closer too.

card.front: The Great Squirrel Incident: negotiations failed
card.back: Reggie: BATTLE. Biscuit: Negotiation failed. Mochi: Squirrel won.

facts: VERIFY: squirrels run along fences and wires, where a dog cannot follow

beats.text:
"OH OH OH, YOU'RE HERE!"
It was the BIGGEST STICK we've ever found!
Chosen by fate!
It was lying in the leaves like it was waiting for ME.
I carried it nearly the whole way.

Well hello, sweet pea. Come in, {name}.
Now this stick.
Remarkable craftsmanship.
A good six feet of oak, straight as a preacher, and the bark, baby, the bark had character.
Reggie found it, but I want you to know that I recognized it first, in my heart.
And then we got to the gate.
The stick had its own opinions about the gate.
Stick.

episodes.evening:
Reggie lay on the porch with his chin on the step.
"It was a good stick."
"Remarkable craftsmanship," said Biscuit.
Mochi did not lift his head.
"Stick."
Reggie smiled.
"The best one."
Mochi, very quietly, scooted over to make room.

card.front: The Stick of Destiny: too wide for the gate
card.back: Reggie: Chosen by fate. Biscuit: Remarkable craftsmanship. Mochi: Stick.

beats.text:
"OKAY, OKAY, OKAY!"
The BEACH!
The sea left, and the whole bottom of it was just THERE.
I tracked a crab for ten minutes, a crab with a plan.
Then it turned out to be a shoe.
A decoy shoe.
That is what I said.

Come on in, {name}. I've got a story for you.
A beautiful afternoon at the shore.
The tide had gone out and left the sand hard and cold and shining.
The gulls were hollerin'.
And the air tasted like salt and seaweed and something that was either a crab or a very old sandwich.
Reggie, lord love him, followed that something for ten solemn minutes, low to the ground, like a detective in a picture show.
Shoe.

episodes.evening:
In the car on the way home, Reggie fell asleep with his head on Biscuit.
Mochi looked out the window.
"Best day of my life," Biscuit whispered.
Mochi did not turn around.
"Fine day."
Then, a little later, "Tide pool was good."

card.front: The beach at low tide: one crab, allegedly a shoe
card.back: Reggie: Decoy shoe. Biscuit: Best day of my life. Mochi: Shoe.

facts: At low tide the sea pulls back and leaves tide pools in the sand

beats.text:
"YOU'RE HERE!"
You will NOT believe where the floor went.
We were on a BOAT, a road that floats, my FIRST boat.
I stood at the rail like a captain.
The nervous human on deck?
I SAVED her.
I leaned on her leg.

Well hello there, {name}. Come in, have a seat.
It was a ferry, and I do not mind sayin' it was the grandest thing.
The whole deck hummed under my paws, a low steady hum I felt in my teeth.
Salt wind.
A little diesel.
And somewhere three rows over, somebody's french fries.
And, baby, the floor moved.
Not much.
Enough.
Mochi sat down flat in the middle of the deck and declared he'd be filing a formal complaint.
Floor moved.

episodes.evening:
That night all three were in a pile on the rug.
"My first boat," said Reggie, to nobody.
"The floor moved," said Mochi.
"It did," said Biscuit.
Mochi sighed.
"Wasn't bad."
Reggie was already asleep, smiling.

card.front: The ferry: a road that floats, officially
card.back: Reggie: Rescued a human. Biscuit: The floor MOVED. Mochi: Floor moved.

facts: A ferry carries people and cars across water
Dogs can feel vibration through their paws

beats.text:
"OKAY, OKAY, OKAY!"
The MARKET!
A whole parking lot of smells!
There was a sad table, a slow morning, and I fixed it.
I sat there and I looked at her and SIX PEOPLE came over.
She sold every peach.
Every one.

Come on in, {name}. I've got a story for you.
Peaches, baby.
Peaches, and warm bread, and a man frying onions in a pan, and a lady with honey you could smell from the car.
A farmers market is the whole world at nose height.
And Reggie, my sweet friend, spotted a vendor having a slow mornin', shoulders down.
He sat himself right in front of her table.
Didn't say a word.
Just looked.
Cheese sample. Acceptable.

episodes.evening:
Reggie told it again at dinner, to the humans, who did not understand a word.
Biscuit narrated over him.
Mochi ate quietly, then looked up.
"Good day."
Reggie stopped mid-sentence and stared at him.
Mochi went back to his bowl.

card.front: The farmers market: one slow table, six new friends
card.back: Reggie: Fixed her morning. Biscuit: PEACHES. Mochi: Cheese sample. Acceptable.

facts: Farmers markets often allow leashed dogs
A dog's nose sits close to the height of market tables
